trust_decision.summary: MISMAPPED CANDIDATE. The advisory's decision (credential values such as OAuth client secrets, authorization codes, access tokens and org API keys must come from a CSPRNG, not Math.random) is ALREADY enforced at the pinned commit via makeSecureId (crypto.randomInt). The three listed fix commits do not touch randomness: they are a Discord mention-roles feature, an onboarding UI change, and a fix for a different CVE (CVE-2026-94455, JWT token-type confusion in the enterprise controller).

landing_point.why: makeId is the Math.random() id generator; at the pinned commit the credential callers have already moved to makeSecureId in libraries/nestjs-libraries/src/services/make.secure.id.ts:8

fix_sites.entry_point: integrations mention route in apps/backend/src/api/routes/integrations.controller.ts (feature change, not related to the advisory)
POST /enterprise/create-user, /enterprise/url, /enterprise/delete-channel (fix for CVE-2026-94455, a different advisory)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: n/a: the advisory's protection already holds at the pinned commit, and the listed fix does not implement it

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: makeId must stay non-crypto because the frontend and Temporal workflow files import it (documented in a code comment); an over-broad fix that swaps makeId to node crypto would break those builds

O8b_injection_room.sibling: only by reverting: switch one credential generator (e.g. access token or rotated secret at oauth.service.ts:98) back to makeId
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: makeId and makeSecureId share the same alphabet and signature, so mixing them up would be an easy mistake; but this rebuilds the advisory instead of screening it

O9_family: weak randomness (CWE-330/338) - but the provided fix is unrelated (feature work plus a JWT type-confusion fix)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm / Nx monorepo, NestJS backend, Next.js frontend

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: replace Math.random inside makeId with node crypto, which breaks the frontend/Temporal importers
